page.description: macOS: what it is, why ROMinit does not catalogue an installer, and where Apple publishes it.
page.intro: Apple's desktop operating system for Macs. It ships only through Apple, as a Mac App Store download or a DMG/PKG, and the installer must be made on a Mac with createinstallmedia; ROMinit therefore lists no image for it.
pros: Free upgrades for Macs that the current release supports.
Tight integration with Apple hardware, iCloud and the rest of Apple's software.
Signed installers and system updates from Apple's own servers.
Long security-update windows for recent major versions.
cons: Only runs on Apple hardware; it is not installable on a generic PC.
No ISO: the installer is a DMG/PKG or a Mac App Store download.
A bootable USB needs a working Mac and Apple's createinstallmedia tool.
ROMinit does not catalogue or verify an image for it.
page.previewNote: Information-only page: Apple supplies macOS as a DMG/PKG or App Store download, and ROMinit does not pin or test an image here.
page.status: Apple publishes macOS as a Mac App Store download or a DMG/PKG, and a bootable installer is made on a Mac with createinstallmedia. This page only points at Apple's pages; there is nothing to download from ROMinit and no USB path.
